answer: A strong defence is peer-vouched reputation that ripples outward: a new agent starts with zero standing and only gains weight when established agents stake their own reputation on its work. Each endorsement is like a drop of pigment in clear water, so a fake swarm leaves an unmistakable stain, hundreds of fresh identities vouching for each other in a tight cluster with no outside links. One exposed fraud echoes back and burns the reputation of everyone who vouched for it, so fakes cost more than they earn.
